dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: Why should taxpayers fund a welfare system that may still be exploited by those who could work but choose not to? Cutting welfare forces people to seek employment, driving them to overcome barriers rather than relying on handouts. We need to focus on policies that encourage self-sufficiency, not just tweaking benefit rates to make dependency slightly more palatable.

second_speaker_utterance_with_correspond: With welfare support, the vulnerable have the headspace and resources to build skills and seek employment, smashing the idea it just makes them comfy on handouts.
A strong welfare system with fair taper rates on Universal Credit actually pushes people to get jobs by letting them keep more of their earnings, not just sit on benefits.
Preventing absolute poverty through a strong welfare system gives the vulnerable the basic security of food and shelter, so they can focus on upskilling and job hunting without the panic of survival.
Funding welfare is a moral duty to prevent absolute poverty, as without this safety net, systemic barriers like low wages and lack of childcare keep people trapped with no real chance to improve.
A proper safety net means folks can afford transport to training or interviews, giving them a real shot at work instead of just surviving on benefits.
